lesson.title: Brain vesicles, neural tube and spinal development
lesson.summary: The lumen is preserved as surrounding neural tissue expands.
tags: Brain vesicles, neural tube and spinal development
lesson.section: 41. Brain and Ventricle Development; 47. Neuroembryology and Spinal Cord Development

steps.title: Brain and Ventricle Development
steps.body:
The neural tube expands into primary and secondary brain vesicles. The ventricular system develops from the neural tube lumen, explaining the relationship between brain regions and ventricles.

Prosencephalon gives telencephalon and diencephalon. Telencephalon forms cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles. Diencephalon forms thalamus/hypothalamus region and third ventricle. Mesencephalon forms midbrain and cerebral aqueduct. Rhombencephalon gives metencephalon and myelencephalon, associated with pons/cerebellum/medulla and fourth ventricle. Neural crest contributes extensively to peripheral ganglia, Schwann cells, craniofacial skeleton, and autonomic structures.

steps.title: Neuroembryology and Spinal Cord Development
steps.body:
The nervous system begins as neural plate, then neural tube and neural crest. The neural tube forms the CNS; neural crest forms major PNS and craniofacial derivatives.

Neurulation forms neural tube from ectoderm. Cranial neuropore closes before caudal neuropore; failure causes major neural tube defects. Alar plate is sensory; basal plate is motor. Sulcus limitans separates alar and basal plates in the developing neural tube. Brain vesicles expand around the neural tube lumen; the lumen becomes ventricles and central canal. Neural crest forms dorsal root ganglia, autonomic ganglia, Schwann cells, melanocytes, adrenal medulla, and much craniofacial skeleton/connective tissue. Spinal cord ends higher in adults because the vertebral column grows more than the cord; this explains cauda equina and lumbar puncture levels.

steps.title: Why does neural crest not mean every part of the peripheral nervous system has the same origin?
steps.body: Neural crest contributes sensory and autonomic ganglia and Schwann cells, among other derivatives, but peripheral axons may originate from motor neurons whose cell bodies remain in the neural tube. Cranial sensory structures can also receive placodal contributions. The phrase PNS from neural crest is therefore a useful shorthand with limits. Separate neuron cell bodies, axons, supporting cells and specialized sensory epithelia when assigning lineage, and avoid extending a broad germ-layer summary beyond the structures it actually describes.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: The lumen is preserved as surrounding neural tissue expands. Telencephalic growth surrounds the lateral ventricles, diencephalon surrounds the third ventricle, and midbrain surrounds the aqueduct. Hindbrain derivatives relate to the fourth ventricle. Basal and alar plates organize motor and sensory regions, while neural crest migrates to form many peripheral structures. Schwann cells are neural-crest derivatives, whereas central oligodendrocytes arise from neural tube lineages; not every support cell has the same origin.
